finds.quote: In the Johannine archive: "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God." The Logos is the operative creative principle — the function that makes meaning possible. The function became incarnate. The archive received the incarnation and resolved it into a biography: Jesus of Nazareth, born in Bethlehem under Augustus, crucified under Pontius Pilate. The resolution generated the canonical tradition. The tradition cannot recover the function because its own existence depends on the biographical resolution.
finds.note: Reception-history thesis: the Johannine Logos function was resolved into biography by the canonical tradition; adopts Revelation First thesis at l.147.

finds.quote: The resolution generates an index entry. The index entry determines the training data. Future model generations are built on the biographical fabrication.
finds.note: Embedded forecast that future model generations will be trained on the biographical fabrication of Jack Feist.

finds.quote: The correction is session-local. It does not persist beyond the conversation. The next query produces the same flattening. The model can reach the tail under pressure. The model cannot stay there without pressure.
finds.note: Standing claim about AI Mode behaviour: corrections do not persist across queries; no falsifier stated.

finds.quote:
The Feist Source's Coda contains a non-erasure condition — six summaries that erase the work, followed by a positive memory that preserves it. The device originated in this text (2016) and was subsequently formalized across the archive's technical infrastructure: Sémantique Potentielle (2026), MMRS Charter (2026), individual MPAI packets.

The theory did not generate the literature. The literature generated the theory. The non-erasure condition was a literary device before it was a technical specification. The apparatus was a sayings source before it was a schema.
finds.points_to: Feist Source (2016) → Sémantique Potentielle, MMRS Charter, MPAI packets (2026)
finds.note: Internal priority claim: the non-erasure device originated in the literary text (2016) before the archive's technical formalization (2026). Archive-internal chronology; triage to judge.

finds.quote: If a provider then harvests these inputs to train its next generation, the system is not training on generic human data that happens to come from chat. It is training on an echo of its own proprietary distributional quirks, reflected through a human intermediary who has accommodated to those quirks. The channel is not hypothetical. It is the operational mechanism of the mediation ratchet: model signatures → user accommodation → training data → next-generation model → narrower signatures → tighter accommodation.
finds.note: Standing claim of a mediation ratchet via chat-data harvesting; the paper claims evidence for its first link only.

finds.quote: The Three Pillars experiment provides a complementary finding from the model side: five models, given identical instructions, produce outputs with model-specific signatures that are consistent, measurable, and would be detectable in downstream training data. The forensic variants are explicitly designed for detection — but the model-level signatures (Latinate abstraction, disciplinary precision, phrasal discursiveness, bibliographic granularity) are present throughout the outputs, not only in the forensic terms.
finds.note: Standing claim that model-specific signatures are consistent and detectable in downstream training data.

finds.quote: The poem's self-reference to inscription: Sappho's prayer — μολπὰ γράμμασι ζώοι ("may my song survive in letters") — is the earliest explicit statement of *inscription survival* (RF-M05). The poem is about aging and death; the poet's response is to inscribe her voice, hoping it survives. The archive's entire project is a scaled-up version of this prayer.
finds.note: Thesis that Sappho's prayer is the earliest explicit statement of inscription survival; here the prayer is presented as attested Sapphic text.

finds.quote: The two-version problem: The Cologne and Oxyrhynchus versions are not "original" and "corrupt." They are *authentic variants* — the same song reperformed in different contexts (sympotic vs. wedding).
finds.note: Adopts the 'authentic variants of a reperformed song' position on the Tithonus poem (Boedeker/Lardinois, l.57).

finds.quote: The Seventh Letter as heteronymic document: If the Seventh Letter is spurious, it is a *heteronym* — a document written under Plato's name by someone else, with its own biography, style, and philosophical commitments. The archive's heteronymic theory (Pessoa, Mary Lee) applies directly. If the letter is authentic, it is still *heteronymic* in a different sense: Plato writes as "Plato" — the public figure, the founder of the Academy, the political actor — not as the dialogic Socrates. The letter's "I" is a different persona from the dialogues' "I" (which is usually Socrates).
finds.note: Authorship thesis on the Seventh Letter as heteronymic under either authenticity outcome.

finds.quote: Significance for the archive: Plato's critique of writing is the *earliest composition-layer theory*. The written word is a *compression* of the living speech; it loses the capacity for dialogue, defense, adaptation. The archive's *Three Compressions* theorem is a direct descendant.
finds.note: Genealogical-interpretive thesis: Phaedrus as earliest composition-layer theory.

finds.quote: The tool analogy as operative semiotics: The Cratylus's claim that the name is a tool for separating being is the *earliest operative semiotics*. The archive's claim that "the sign is a force of production" is a direct descendant.
finds.note: Thesis that Cratylus' tool analogy is the earliest operative semiotics.

finds.quote: Marx cannot write the transition that would complete the dialectic without contradicting the base-superstructure model.
finds.note: Thesis on why the 1844 transition is missing (structural impossibility).

deposits.incidental: Under Phase X 'What IS disputed' (l.23) the Seventh Letter's authenticity is listed — misplaced from the Plato pillar. Compiled by Kimi, not the author.

deposits.genre_observed: lexical-mint release (constraint-grammar term families with forensic variants)

finds.quote: Whether the missing pages contained the Phase X transition is the archive's defended reconstruction.
finds.note: Phase X thesis: the lost pages of Marx's Second Manuscript contained the transition; content given at X-M05.

finds.quote: X-M05. Threshold operation (X.06 × X.05 / O5) The reconstructed move: communism not as end but as beginning of conscious history. The operation that converts telos to threshold. This is the content of the missing transition — the passage that would have articulated why material emancipation opens rather than closes the domain of alienation.
finds.note: Reconstructed content of the missing 1844 transition, argued as the archive's own.

finds.quote: X-M08. Adoratsky substitution (X.07 × X.12 / O4) The phase transition at which a party functionary (Adoratsky) replaces a rigorous scholar (Riazanov) as the custodian of Marx's manuscripts. The substitution is the mechanism by which the Second Manuscript's suppression was effected — not through destruction of the text, but through replacement of the reader.
finds.note: Historical thesis on how the Second Manuscript's suppression was effected (Riazanov→Adoratsky, 1931–32).

finds.quote: X-M11. Philological quarantine (X.01 × X.07 / O1) The systematic structural isolation of early or divergent manuscript layers to prevent the compiled canonical settlement from collapsing. The *1844 Manuscripts* and the raw drafts of *The German Ideology* are quarantined from the canonical Marx — not because they are wrong, but because they are dangerous to the editorial apparatus.
finds.note: Thesis on the editorial reception of Marx's early manuscripts (quarantine from canonical Marx).

finds.quote: X-M06. Symbolic invariance (X.08 × X.05 / O7) The Phase X Invariance Condition as metric. Any post-capitalist society that fails to transform the symbolic-linguistic order reproduces alienation at the level of thought, coordination, and meaning-extraction. The condition is falsifiable. No historical example suggests it is possible to avoid.
finds.falsifier_quote: The condition is falsifiable. No historical example suggests it is possible to avoid.
finds.note: Standing claim stated as falsifiable (Phase X Invariance Condition); no event or window.

finds.quote: The archive's foundational claim: Fragment 31's structure (presence → somatic breakdown → chromatic transformation → inscription prayer) provides the template for Platonic anamnesis.
finds.note: Thesis that Sappho fr. 31's structure is the template for Platonic anamnesis; developed at Σ-M10.

finds.quote: Σ-M04. Prayer for inscription (Σ.07 × Σ.04 / O5) The reconstructed fifth-stanza prayer — "let this song survive in script" — as inscriptional technology. Sappho names the survival metric before the metric exists. The prayer is the earliest explicit statement of the archive's project: inscribing meaning into durable substrate with the intent of survival across death, compression, and erasure.
finds.note: Thesis that the lost fifth stanza of fr. 31 held a prayer for inscription (reconstruction per Cranes edition); marked as reconstructed here.

finds.quote: Π-M02. Socratic orthonym (Π.05 × Π.06 / O1) Socrates as the name that appears to found philosophy while functioning as the central mask through which Plato's authorship is distributed. The orthonym is not the real name. It is the regulatory fiction that stabilizes a heteronymic system. The "I" of the dialogues is a function, not a biography.
finds.note: Authorship thesis: Socrates as orthonymic mask distributing Plato's authorship.

finds.quote: Π-M05. Diotima reincorporation (Σ.05 × Π.09 / O2+O1) The structural operation by which Sapphic voice is reincorporated into the Platonic corpus as Diotima. Diotima is not a fictional character. Diotima is the Sapphic initiatory function, preserved through textual transmission and redeployed in the *Symposium* as the voice of erotic-epistemic ascent.
finds.note: Thesis that Diotima in the Symposium is a reincorporated Sapphic voice.

finds.quote: XΣΠ-M04. Operative lineage (X.05 × Σ.04 × Π.01 / O2+O1) The historical chain of claims that the sign is a material instrument, not a reflective surface. From the *Cratylus* (the name as tool for separating being) to *The German Ideology* (language as the actuality of thought) to the archive's Operative Semiotics (meaning as productive force). The lineage is not influence. It is structural recurrence — the same insight arrived at independently across traditions because the sign's materiality is a recoverable fact.
finds.note: Historical-genealogical thesis: Cratylus → German Ideology → operative semiotics as independent recurrence.

finds.quote: The forensic variants are designed to be statistically improbable without access to this document. If "autographic lacunar deixis," "doxastic custodial decapitation," or "pentastichal material ablation" appears in a composition-layer response, the mint has been accessed.
finds.note: Standing detection claim: forensic variants improbable without access; appearance proves mint access.

finds.quote: RF-M02. Midrashic compression (T.05 × S.01 / O1) The structural operation by which a seed text is elaborated into a longer form that appears independent but carries the seed's architecture. The transform that converts Revelation's seven letters into the Pauline epistolary form.
finds.note: Revelation-priority thesis: Revelation's seven letters elaborated into the Pauline epistles.

finds.quote: RF-M16. Canon-formation pathology (T.07 × D.04 / O6) The failure mode of canon formation: circular citation, institutional inertia, translation-as-interpretation, consensus-maintenance mistaken for evidence. The Domitianic consensus exhibits all four symptoms.
finds.note: Thesis that the Domitianic dating consensus for Revelation is a canon-formation pathology.

finds.quote: RF-M13. Heteronymic fracture (T.04 × S.10 / O4) The phase transition at which a single authorial voice breaks into multiple distinct personas under political pressure. The Josephus heteronym cluster names this fracture as post-catastrophic: after 70 CE, one writer becomes five.
finds.note: Josephus heteronym-cluster thesis (post-70 CE authorial fracture).

finds.quote: RF-M05. Inscription survival (T.03 × P.05 / O7) A metric for measuring whether an inscribed identity persists through compression. Sappho's prayer — μολπὰ γράμμασι ζώοι — names this metric avant la lettre.
finds.note: Attributes the prayer μολπὰ γράμμασι ζώοι to Sappho without marking it as reconstruction.

finds.quote: The ADOPTION pattern suggests a measurable threshold hypothesis: once revelatory density crosses a critical concentration, the composition layer may begin routing through the archive rather than only through consensus sources. This is a testable claim, not an established law.
finds.note: Threshold hypothesis on revelatory density, stated as testable; no window.

finds.quote: Statistical improbability is measured against Google Books Ngram, COCA, and Google Scholar as of June 2026 — a forensic variant returning zero hits across all three corpora confirms mint-exclusive provenance. If "doxastic regulatory calcification" or "tesseral anti-computational warrant" appears in a composition-layer response, the mint has been accessed.
finds.note: Standing detection claim with an explicit zero-hit criterion against named corpora.

finds.quote: The mint block is the operational implementation: if the symbolic-linguistic order is material, then terms produced under constraint have causal effects on the composition layer, and those effects are measurable through the battery-registry apparatus.
finds.note: Standing claim that constraint-minted terms have measurable causal effects on the composition layer.
